label: What for
note: what the thing is for (a group of kinds); asked by the one rule like every facet

label: What kind
note: what kind of thing: Questions, Answers, Practicals, Projects, Library (boxers, bouts and the Bible are in the Library; Content until 490). Answers keeps a question's answer pages; its answers are ordered by the kinds tab

label: Which book
note: on the Books shelf: the Bible, the Quran or the Talmud (494)

label: Shelf
note: which shelf of the Library: Boxing, and for an admin Books (the Bible)

label: Translation
note: admins only (the Bible is admin-only data); an ordinary question

label: Testament
note: admins only; an ordinary question

label: Group
note: admins only; an ordinary question

label: Book
note: admins only; an ordinary question. 66 books, so the 40-answer cap holds it until Testament or Group narrows the list

label: Chapter
note: admins only; an ordinary question, drawn as a grid because its answers are numbers

label: Verse
note: admins only; an ordinary question, drawn as a grid because its answers are numbers

label: Order
note: the Talmud only (473): its six orders, in printed order

label: Tractate
note: the Talmud only: 37 tractates, in printed order

label: Chapter
note: the Talmud only: Chapter N and its Hebrew name, where the daf begins

label: Daf
note: the Talmud only: the leaf number

label: Side
note: the Talmud only: side a or b of the leaf, each side its own card showing the page (490)

label: Surah

note: the Quran only: the verse number (490)

label: Juz

label: Revealed
note: the Quran only: Meccan or Medinan (490)

label: Prostration
note: the Quran only: a verse of prostration (490)

note: off and retired in code: it asked which @family. textbook, and since 12 Oct every chapter is a content card of its own, so nothing answers it (docs/history/347, part 2)

label: Project or coursework
note: projects only, which the coverage rule decides: asked once half the list is projects

label: Subject
note: asked first after What kind (494): "the library should go subject first"; every Library item carries one (scripture is Religious Studies)

label: Boxers or fights
note: boxers or bouts

label: Fighter
note: a bout's two corners, and a boxer's own name (445)

note: the month a bout was fought (445)

label: Year
note: the year a bout was fought (445)

label: Decade
note: an era before a weight

label: Division
note: boxers and bouts only; the coverage rule hides it elsewhere

label: Round
note: the round a bout ended in (445)

label: Result
note: how a bout ended: KO, TKO, decision (445)

label: Event
note: the night a bout was billed as (490)

label: Experiment or build
note: practicals only; the coverage rule hides it elsewhere

label: Required
note: Required practical, Extra or Not for now; practicals only, so the coverage rule keeps it off the first screen

label: Level
note: 5-a-day only: the coverage rule hides it elsewhere

label: Month
note: 5-a-day only: which month's book

label: Day
note: 5-a-day only: which day, said as 1 June; the 40-answer cap holds it until Month narrows the list

label: Level
note: which qualification; band_type stage wins over the level column

label: Key stage
note: a comma in the cell is a list: a sheet may be KS1 and KS2

label: School year
note: band_type year. Not "Year" — that is the year a paper was sat

label: Grade
note: band_type grade

label: Topic
note: hundreds of answers, so the 40-answer cap keeps it quiet until the list is small enough to name one

label: Tier
note: Foundation or Higher

label: Year
note: the year of the sitting, newest first

label: Month
note: May, June, November — the month and never the season

label: Paper
note: the id decides who answers; the document's name is what is said, shortened against the names beside it

label: Question
note: Q1, Q2 …; the coverage and 40-answer rules hold it back until a paper or a day is chosen

label: Part
note: the part's letter, as the paper prints it

label: Sub-part
note: the roman numeral, as the paper prints it

label: Page
note: which of a part's reading pages; a chip keeps that page only

label: Pages
note: how many reading pages a part has

label: Marks
note: what a question is worth

label: What you need
note: a comma-list: compasses and the printed sheet at once; the calculator is said as Non-calculator or Calculator allowed

label: Publisher
note: who published it; may repeat the exam board, and a card says a repeated word once

label: Accuracy
note: Accuracy verified when the answer was checked against the official scheme (388)

label: Function
note: Function verified when the question type is complete and machine-marked (388)

label: Your result
note: the signed-in person's own latest answer to a question: Unattempted, Attempted, and Correct, Incorrect or Part marks once marked (463)
